title: Baltimore Ravens vs. Atlanta Falcons Postgame Analysis: What Happened, What We Got Right and What We Learned

excerpt: Baltimore Ravens won 30-23. THE NUMBER LANDED AND THE REASONING DID NOT. This is the most dangerous result on this page, because it pays and teaches nothing. Nothing below should be read as EdgeDesk having understood this game.
seo_description: Baltimore Ravens beat Atlanta Falcons 30-23. EdgeDesk’s number implied Baltimore Ravens +3.5 — win. 6 of 12 gradeable claims held up, 5 did not. Process grade: UNSOUND. Research, not picks.

implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 3.7 points toward Baltimore Ravens of the quote EdgeDesk captured at Caesars. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 47.2 sat 3.7 points above the captured total of 43.5.

closing_line.note: The line moved 0.3 points toward the side EdgeDesk’s number leaned before kickoff. That is the market arriving where EdgeDesk already was, and over many games it is the only evidence that a disagreement carried information.

reasons: 5 of 10 gradeable claims went the other way. The read of this matchup was wrong in its mechanism, not only in its number.
The result carries 1 high-variance marker — 1 defensive touchdown — so the scoreboard is weaker evidence than it looks.
EdgeDesk projected a away margin of 0.2 and the game finished 7 the away way — 6.8 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.

lessons.suggested_investigation: Why did the number land while the mechanism failed? Either the number was right for a reason EdgeDesk has not identified, or it was luck. Both are worth knowing and they are different.
